body: test-sprints-write-tests-that-wait-on-the-wall-clock: Judgment issue about the project's own tooling (category tooling); the fix lies in files this repo owns as the suite's source under plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/, so route question, not upstream. EVIDENCE, re-verified: the testing standard and the old coding rule are gone and nothing replaced them. Release v22.0.0 (b98a091) deleted plugins/ok/families/ok-plumbline/docs/testing.md (ROT: the filed problem names plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/testing.md; the file lived under ok-plumbline). plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/ now holds events.md, plumbline-cheatsheet.md, plumbline-coding.md, practice-definitions.md, stack-helpers.md, technical-writing.md, shapes/; no testing document. Rule 7 of plumbline-coding.md is now 'Enumerate the inputs a command accepts'; the only clock rule left is 3.6 'Elapsed time is computed from one clock' (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/plumbline-coding.md:35), which governs product code, not test waits. {{TEST-WRITE-PROMPT}} at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:764 says 'Reach the code through its public entry point ... Mock nothing the scenario checks' and nothing on sleeps, polls, or waits; a grep of skills/plan-tests/ for sleep|poll|elapsed|wall clock|deadline finds nothing. The fix prompt (core.md:973) refuses a fix that hides a failure behind 'a longer timeout, or a retry'; the verify prompt (core.md:1041) sends back 'a longer timeout, a retry with no budget'. Both read fixes only; a test written to sleep from the start passes both. NEW since filing (ROT: 'nothing measures how long a test takes'): testing.timeout now exists, a per-test limit in seconds (SKILL.md:28-32, scripts/tests:291, default 600), and planning checks each planned kind and setup pair ends within it (SKILL.md:82-84). It caps one test; it measures no round and forbids no sleep. MECHANISM: (1) a test sprint's writers get no rule on how a test waits, so they default to sleep-and-poll; (2) the verifier reads only fixes, so no reader checks a test's waits. CORPUS: decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests lists the verifier's send-back reasons ('hides a failure behind a swallowing catch, a longer timeout, or a blind retry') and has it read 'each fix'; a verifier that also reads tests for sleeps widens that decision, a corpus delta. decision:tests-check-scenarios names 'time' among runtime classes and is silent on how a test waits. decision:test-sprints-own-the-tests is silent. No story or decision forbids wall-clock waits in tests. TOOLING the change would edit: plan-tests/core.md ({{TEST-WRITE-PROMPT}}, the fix and verify prompts), plan-tests/SKILL.md, the cheatsheet source docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md Tests section, possibly docs/plumbline-coding.md, and for option C scripts/tests (complete) and the testing config. HARM: no accept-list entry covers a slow or flaky suite as such; it is a tooling quality question, so no generated ruling. OPTIONS: A, restore the standard as a suite document under docs/, condense it into the cheatsheet's Tests section, cite it from the write, fix, and verify prompts, and have the verifier send back a test or fix that sleeps or polls on elapsed time; cost: one more standards document, a corpus delta to decision:test-loop-fixes-code-never-tests, and a verify pass that reads tests as well as fixes. B, put the rules in the write, fix, and verify prompts alone; cost: the rule binds only test-sprint agents, and the cheatsheet's Tests section stays silent for anyone else. C, do A and add a round budget beside testing.timeout, with tests complete refusing a round over budget; cost: a wider testing config and a completion check that depends on the machine. MISSED option D: a mechanical check, a test-sprint step or project check that greps the written tests for sleep and deadline reads and fails the write task; cost: language-specific patterns and false hits on legitimate fake-clock sleeps. Note the owner's linescout project already carries the restored text as a project rule, .claude/rules/tests-wait-on-events.md, which is a source for option A's text. No stated rule decides among the options. SIBLINGS: none open.
